items.name: Empirical
items.workup: Prior to culture results — change once cultures are final.
items.aetiology: Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Gram-negative bacilli
items.first: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (if penicillin allergic)
items.second: If recent hospitalization/antibiotics/septic shock: vancomycin 1g IV BD + piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h, OR + cefepime 2g IV q8h (penicillin allergic); switch to meropenem if previous ESBL, contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

items.name: Pathogen-directed — S. aureus (MSSA)
items.workup: 2 sets blood cultures q48h until negative, ECHO to r/o IE, identify source, remove central line, contact ID/Clinical Microbiology
items.first: Cefazolin 2g IV q8h OR Cloxacillin 2g IV q4h
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD (if unavailable/penicillin allergic)
items.duration: Depends on ECHO result and 1st negative blood culture

items.name: Pathogen-directed — S. aureus (MRSA)
items.first: Vancomycin 20mg/kg loading then 15mg/kg IV BD; trough before 4th dose, target 15–20
items.duration: Depends on ECHO result and 1st negative blood culture

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Streptococcal sp.
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD, trough before 4th dose
items.duration: Depends on ECHO result and 1st negative blood culture

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Pseudomonas aeruginosa
items.first: Cefepime 2g IV q8h (penicillin allergic) OR Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h
items.second: Meropenem if ESBL

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Enterococcus sp.
items.first: Vancomycin 1g IV BD (penicillin allergic), trough target 10–15
items.second: Ampicillin 2g IV q4h if ampicillin-sensitive
items.duration: Depends on ECHO result and 1st negative blood culture

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Candida sp.
items.workup: Same workup + ophthalmology consult to r/o endophthalmitis
items.aetiology: C. albicans, glabrata, parapsilosis, tropicalis, auris
items.first: Anidulafungin 200mg loading then 100mg IV OD OR Caspofungin 70mg loading then 50mg IV OD
items.second: If unavailable, transfer to MOH
items.duration: Depends on ECHO result and 1st negative blood culture

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Salmonella sp.
items.workup: Higher resistance risk if recent travel Pakistan/SE Asia/Africa; more common in children, immunocompromised, HIV, liver disease, sickle cell
items.first: Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV BD (penicillin allergic) OR Levofloxacin 750mg IV OD
items.second: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD OR Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD; if recent travel start meropenem, adjust per culture
items.duration: 14 days (no extra-intestinal focus); 4–6 weeks if extra-intestinal (mycotic aneurysm, osteomyelitis)

items.name: Empirical
items.aetiology: S. aureus, Streptococcus sp., Enterococcus sp.
items.first: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (add gentamicin + rifampin if prosthetic valve)

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Native valve, HACEK organisms
items.aetiology: H. parainfluenzae, Eikenella corrodens, Kingella sp., Bartonella sp., Cardiobacterium, Aggregatibacter sp.
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD
items.second: Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Native valve, Streptococcus sp.
items.workup: Remove central line, repeat blood culture q2-3d until negative
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD OR Ampicillin 2g IV q4h
items.second: Vancomycin 15–20mg/kg IV BD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Native valve, S. aureus (MSSA)
items.first: Cefazolin 2g IV q8h OR Cloxacillin 2g IV q4h
items.second: Vancomycin 15–20mg/kg IV BD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Native valve, S. aureus (MRSA)
items.first: Vancomycin 20mg/kg loading then 15mg/kg IV BD, trough 15–20

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Native valve, Enterococcus faecium
items.first: Vancomycin 20mg/kg loading then 15mg/kg IV BD + gentamicin 1mg/kg q8h, trough 15–20

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Native valve, Enterococcus faecalis
items.first: Ampicillin 2g IV q4h + Ceftriaxone 2g IV q12h (if ampicillin-sensitive; if not, give vancomycin)
items.second: Vancomycin 20mg/kg loading then 15mg/kg IV BD, trough 15–20 (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Native valve, Candida sp.
items.workup: Ophthalmology consult; contact isolation if C. auris
items.aetiology: C. albicans, tropicalis, parapsilosis, glabrata, auris
items.first: Anidulafungin 200mg IV OD
items.second: Caspofungin 150mg IV OD

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Prosthetic valve, HACEK organisms
items.first: Same regimen as native valve

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Prosthetic valve, Streptococcus sp.
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD
items.second: Vancomycin 20mg/kg loading then 15mg/kg IV BD, trough 15–20

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Prosthetic valve, S. aureus (MSSA)
items.first: Cefazolin 2g IV q8h + gentamicin + rifampin OR Cloxacillin 2g IV q4h + gentamicin + rifampin
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + gentamicin + rifampin

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Prosthetic valve, S. aureus (MRSA)
items.first: Vancomycin 20mg/kg loading then 15mg/kg IV BD + gentamicin + rifampin, trough 15–20

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Prosthetic valve, Enterococcus faecalis
items.first: Ampicillin 2g IV q4h + gentamicin 1mg/kg q8h (if ampicillin-sensitive)
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + gentamicin 1mg/kg q8h

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Prosthetic valve, Enterococcus faecium
items.first: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + gentamicin 1mg/kg q8h
items.second: Daptomycin 8–12mg/kg IV OD if vancomycin-resistant

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Prosthetic valve, Candida sp.
items.first: Anidulafungin 200mg IV OD
items.second: Caspofungin 150mg IV OD

items.name: Bacterial Pericarditis
items.workup: Requires drainage and culture; adjust per culture
items.first: Vancomycin + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD

items.name: Empirical — Community-acquired
items.workup: Age 1 month–50 years, or elderly / immunocompromised. Send CSF studies incl. culture and HSV PCR
items.first: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Add acyclovir if HSV suspected; add ampicillin 2g IV q4h if considering Listeria

items.name: Pathogen-directed — S. pneumoniae
items.first: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV BD + Moxifloxacin 400mg IV OD

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Herpes simplex virus
items.first: Acyclovir 10mg/kg IV q8h
items.second: Acyclovir until improvement then Valacyclovir 1000mg PO q8h to complete

items.name: Pathogen-directed — N. meningitidis
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Pathogen-directed — Listeria monocytogenes
items.first: Ampicillin 2g IV q4h

items.name: Pathogen-directed — H. influenzae
items.first: Dexamethasone 0.15mg/kg q6h before/with 1st dose + Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD

items.name: Empirical — Post-basilar skull fracture (CSF leak)
items.aetiology: H. influenzae, S. pneumoniae, S. pyogenes, N. meningitidis
items.first: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Empirical — Catheter/shunt-related
items.aetiology: Coagulase-neg staph, S. aureus, Gram-negative bacilli
items.first: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV BD + Cefepime 2g IV q8h (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Brain Abscess
items.workup: Drain and culture; adjust per culture
items.aetiology: Streptococcus sp., S. aureus, Bacteroides, Enterobacteriaceae, Nocardia
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD OR Cefotaxime 2g IV q4h + metronidazole (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Cefepime 2g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h; add vancomycin if MRSA positive

items.name: Brain Abscess — Post-traumatic or Post-surgical
items.aetiology: Streptococcus sp., S. aureus, Anaerobes, Enterobacteriaceae, Coag-neg staph
items.first: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h + Cefepime 2g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h + Meropenem 2g IV q8h

items.name: Acute Dacryocystitis
items.aetiology: Streptococcus sp., S. aureus, H. influenzae, Enterobacteriaceae
items.first: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 1 tab q12h OR IV 1.2g q8h OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD (severe/penicillin allergy)

items.name: Preseptal Cellulitis
items.aetiology: Streptococcus sp., S. aureus, H. influenzae, Anaerobes, M. catarrhalis
items.first: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 1 tab q12h OR IV 1.2g q8h OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1–2 DS tab PO BD

items.name: Orbital Cellulitis — Severe or h/o MRSA
items.aetiology: Streptococcus sp., S. aureus, H. influenzae, Anaerobes, M. catarrhalis
items.first: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + Metronidazole 1g IV BD
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h

items.name: Orbital Cellulitis — Mild, no concern for MRSA
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Augmentin 1 tablet PO BD

items.name: Orbital fracture / penetrating trauma with metallic or intraocular foreign body
items.aetiology: Streptococcus sp., S. aureus, H. influenzae, Anaerobes, M. catarrhalis
items.first: Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV BD
items.second: Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD

items.name: Retinitis — HSV, VZV
items.aetiology: Herpes simplex virus, Varicella zoster virus
items.first: Acyclovir 10–12mg/kg IV q8h
items.second: Valganciclovir Oral 1g q8h

items.name: Retinitis — Cytomegalovirus
items.first: Ganciclovir 5mg/kg IV q12h (2–3 weeks), then Valganciclovir 900mg PO OD

items.name: Gastroenteritis — Mild/moderate (outpatient)
items.first: Symptomatic treatment only; no antibiotics indicated

items.name: Gastroenteritis — Moderate/severe
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD OR Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD (also if penicillin allergic)
items.second: Azithromycin 500mg PO OD

items.name: Clostridium difficile
items.first: Oral vancomycin 125mg PO q6h
items.second: Oral vancomycin 500mg PO q6h if severe

items.name: Perforated Appendicitis/Abscess — Mild/moderate
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg PO q8h OR Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV BD + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Moxifloxacin 400mg IV/PO OD

items.name: Perforated Appendicitis/Abscess — Severe: peritonitis/septic shock
items.first: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h OR Cefepime 2g IV q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Meropenem 1g IV q8h if ESBL

items.name: Severe Cholangitis
items.first: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h OR Cefepime 2g q12h + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Meropenem 1g IV q8h OR Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD

items.name: Acute Cholecystitis
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h OR Cefepime 2g q12h + metronidazole
items.second: Ciprofloxacin + metronidazole OR Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h

items.name: Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis
items.aetiology: E. coli, Enterobacteriaceae, Enterococcus sp., Streptococcus sp.
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD OR Cefotaxime 2g IV q8h
items.second: Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV BD OR Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h

items.name: Pancreatitis
items.first: No antimicrobial treatment needed; supportive care only

items.name: Acute Severe Necrotizing Pancreatitis/Abscess
items.first: Ciprofloxacin + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h

items.name: Perirectal Abscess
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD OR Ciprofloxacin + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h
items.second: Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD OR Cefepime 2g IV q12h + metronidazole 1g IV q12h

items.name: Diverticulitis — Outpatient (mild)
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD OR Ciprofloxacin + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h
items.second: Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD

items.name: Diverticulitis — Inpatient, mild/moderate
items.first: Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD OR Ciprofloxacin + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h
items.second: Cefepime 2g IV q12h +/- metronidazole

items.name: Diverticulitis — Inpatient, severe
items.first: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h OR Cefepime 2g IV q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Meropenem 1g IV q8h if ESBL

items.name: Liver Abscess
items.aetiology: Klebsiella sp., Bacteroides sp., Enterobacteriaceae, Enterococcus sp.
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: If severe: Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375g IV q6h OR Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV BD + metronidazole

items.name: Gastric Ulcer (H. pylori)
items.first: Pylera + PPI
items.second: PPI + Augmentin 1g PO BD + metronidazole + clarithromycin 500mg PO BD

items.name: Asymptomatic Bacteriuria/Candiduria
items.workup: Treat only if pregnant or undergoing invasive urologic procedure
items.aetiology: E. coli, Gram-negative bacilli, Enterococcus sp.
items.first: No need to treat; if foley present, change/remove — no new culture unless symptomatic

items.name: Lower UTI/Cystitis
items.workup: Send urine analysis, then culture if positive
items.aetiology: S. agalactiae, E. coli, Klebsiella sp., Enterococcus sp.
items.first: Nitrofurantoin 100mg PO BD OR Augmentin 1 tab PO BD
items.second: Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab BD OR Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Complicated UTI
items.workup: Change foley if present; culture only if symptomatic
items.aetiology: S. agalactiae, E. coli, Klebsiella sp., Enterococcus sp.
items.first: Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab BD OR Cefepime 2g IV BD OR Piperacillin-Tazobactam (if prior resistance/recent admission)

items.name: Pyelonephritis — Low risk of resistance
items.aetiology: E. coli, Klebsiella sp., Proteus, Enterococcus sp.
items.first: Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab BD

items.name: Pyelonephritis — High risk of resistance
items.first: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h OR Cefepime 2g IV BD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Meropenem 1g IV q8h if ESBL

items.name: Prostatitis
items.aetiology: E. coli, Klebsiella sp., Pseudomonas, Enterococcus sp.
items.first: Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD OR Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD OR Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab BD

items.name: Epididymitis-Orchitis
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD OR Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD

items.name: Intrapartum Group B Strep
items.first: Ampicillin 2g IV loading then 1g IV q4h until delivery
items.second: Clindamycin 900mg IV q8h until delivery

items.name: C-section: Elective and Emergency
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV single dose
items.second: Clindamycin 900mg IV single dose

items.name: Premature Membrane Rupture
items.aetiology: Chlamydia trachomatis, Ureaplasma, S. pneumoniae, Anaerobes
items.first: Azithromycin 1g PO x1 + Ampicillin 2g IV q6h x48h then Amoxicillin 250mg PO q8h x5 days
items.second: Azithromycin 1g PO x1 + clindamycin

items.name: Amnionitis, Septic Abortion
items.aetiology: Chlamydia trachomatis, Ureaplasma, Streptococcus sp., Bacteroides, Enterobacteriaceae, Mycoplasma sp.
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + clindamycin 900mg IV q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: If septic: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h; if previous ESBL: meropenem 1g IV q8h

items.name: Lower UTI/Cystitis (Pregnancy)
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD
items.second: Cefuroxime 500mg PO BD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Catheter-Associated UTI (Pregnancy)
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Cefepime 1g IV q8h

items.name: Syphilis in Pregnancy
items.first: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM
items.second: If unavailable, refer to Infectious Disease hospital

items.name: Vulvovaginitis — Uncomplicated candidiasis
items.first: Fluconazole 150mg PO x1 dose
items.second: Clotrimazole pessaries 500mg single dose

items.name: Vulvovaginitis — Complicated candidiasis (severe/recurrent/immunocompromised)
items.first: Fluconazole 150mg PO q72h

items.name: Bacterial Vaginosis
items.first: Metronidazole 500mg PO q12h
items.second: Clindamycin 300mg PO BD

items.name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease — Outpatient
items.workup: Cervical NAAT for C. trachomatis/N. gonorrhea; drain/culture if tubo-ovarian abscess
items.aetiology: N. gonorrheae, C. trachomatis, Bacteroides sp., E. coli, Klebsiella, Streptococcus sp.
items.first: Ceftriaxone 1g IV OD + doxycycline 100mg PO BD + metronidazole 500mg IV BD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Ceftriaxone 500mg IM/IV x1 + metronidazole 500mg PO BD + doxycycline 100mg PO BD

items.name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease — Inpatient
items.first: Clindamycin 900mg IV q8h + gentamicin 2mg/kg loading then 1.5mg/kg q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Once stable: clindamycin 450mg PO q6h OR doxycycline 100mg PO BD

items.name: Genital Herpes — Initial episode
items.first: Acyclovir 400mg PO q8h

items.name: Genital Herpes — Subsequent episodes
items.first: Acyclovir 800mg PO q8h x2 days
items.second: Acyclovir 400mg PO q8h x5 days

items.name: Urethritis/Cervicitis — Chlamydia, Gonorrhea
items.first: Ceftriaxone 1g IM x1 + doxycycline 100mg PO BD x7 days

items.name: Urethritis/Cervicitis — Trichomonas
items.first: Metronidazole 500mg PO BD

items.name: Syphilis — Primary
items.first: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM, single dose
items.second: If unavailable, refer to Infectious Disease hospital

items.name: Syphilis — Secondary/Late latent (>12 months)
items.first: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM, 1 dose/week x3 weeks
items.second: If unavailable, refer to Infectious Disease hospital

items.name: Contiguous focus
items.workup: Debridement, tissue/bone culture, adjust per culture
items.aetiology: S. aureus, Coag-neg staph, Enterobacteriaceae, Pseudomonas, Streptococcus
items.first: Empiric: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Cefepime 2g IV BD; if sensitive, switch to ciprofloxacin 750mg IV/PO BD or levofloxacin 750mg IV/PO OD

items.name: Hematogenous spread to vertebra or long bones
items.aetiology: S. aureus, Coag-neg staph, Gram-negative bacilli, Salmonella (sickle cell), Streptococcus sp.
items.first: Empiric: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Cefepime 2g IV BD; switch per sensitivity

items.name: Vertebral Osteomyelitis
items.aetiology: S. aureus, Gram-negative bacilli, Streptococcus sp.
items.first: Empiric: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Cefepime 2g IV BD

items.name: Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), Streptococcus sp.
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Cefotaxime 2g IV q8h

items.name: Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)
items.first: Vancomycin 20mg/kg loading then 15mg/kg IV BD, trough 15–20

items.name: Empiric therapy
items.workup: Debridement, culture, remove hardware if possible
items.aetiology: S. aureus, S. epidermidis, Streptococcus sp., Gram-negative bacilli
items.first: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Vancomycin + Ciprofloxacin 750mg PO BD or levofloxacin 750mg PO OD, OR + Cefepime 2g IV BD

items.name: Pharyngitis — Viral
items.aetiology: Enterovirus, ECHO, Coxsackie, EBV, Adenovirus, Influenza, SARS-CoV-2, RSV
items.first: No antibiotics; symptomatic treatment only

items.name: Pharyngitis — Streptococcus pyogenes
items.first: Amoxicillin 500mg PO q8h OR Augmentin 1 tab PO BD OR Clindamycin 300mg PO q8h
items.second: Azithromycin 500mg PO OD x5 days (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Sinusitis — Acute Viral Rhinosinusitis
items.first: Oral fluids and nasal saline irrigation

items.name: Sinusitis — Bacterial
items.aetiology: Streptococcus spp., H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis
items.first: Amoxicillin 500mg PO q8h OR Augmentin 875/125mg PO BD

items.name: Peritonsillar Abscess
items.aetiology: S. aureus, Streptococcus sp., Fusobacterium necrophorum, H. influenzae, Anaerobes
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h OR Clindamycin 600mg IV q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h

items.name: Ludwig's Angina
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h OR Levofloxacin 750mg IV OD + clindamycin 600mg IV q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Vancomycin if S. aureus

items.name: Oropharyngeal Candidiasis — Mild
items.first: Nystatin suspension

items.name: Oropharyngeal Candidiasis — Moderate/Severe
items.first: Fluconazole 100–200mg PO OD

items.name: Otitis Media — Viral
items.first: No antibiotics needed; supportive care

items.name: Otitis Media — Bacterial
items.aetiology: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis
items.first: Augmentin 1g PO BD
items.second: Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Malignant Otitis Externa
items.workup: Requires surgical debridement, culture; may need CT/MRI if severe
items.first: Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD OR Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD
items.second: If severe: Cefepime 2g IV q8h OR Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h OR Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q8h

items.name: Community Acquired Pneumonia — Outpatient, no comorbidities
items.workup: Calculate CURB-65 (Confusion/Urea>7mmol-L/RR≥30/BP<90-60/Age≥65 = 1pt each; 0-1 outpatient, 2 admit-short/monitor, 3 admit, 4-5 admit±ICU)
items.aetiology: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis
items.first: Augmentin 1g PO BD OR Cefuroxime 500mg PO BD
items.second: Azithromycin 500mg PO x1 then 250mg q24h x4 days OR Doxycycline 100mg PO BD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Community Acquired Pneumonia — Outpatient, with comorbidities
items.aetiology: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis
items.first: Augmentin 1g PO BD OR Cefuroxime 500mg PO BD + Azithromycin 500mg x1 then 250mg OD x4d
items.second: Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD OR Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Community Acquired Pneumonia — In-patient
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD OR Cefotaxime 2g IV q8h + Azithromycin 500mg x1 then 250mg OD x4d
items.second: Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD OR Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Community Acquired Pneumonia — Suspected MRSA
items.workup: Previous MRSA culture or positive screen
items.first: Vancomycin (per protocol / contact ID/Clinical Microbiology) OR Linezolid 600mg PO BD
items.second: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab PO BD OR Doxycycline 100mg PO BD

items.name: Community Acquired Pneumonia — Suspected Pseudomonas
items.workup: CF, COPD, Bronchiectasis, or previous Pseudomonas culture
items.first: Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD OR Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD (also if penicillin allergic)
items.second: If severe: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h OR Cefepime 2g IV q8h

items.name: Secondary bacterial pneumonia — post Influenza/COVID
items.first: Vancomycin (per protocol / contact ID/Clinical Microbiology)
items.second: Linezolid 600mg PO BD

items.name: Viral pneumonia — COVID-19
items.first: Supportive care; no antibiotics; transfer to MOH for further management

items.name: Viral pneumonia — Influenza
items.first: Oseltamivir 75mg PO BD + supportive care; no antibiotics

items.name: Viral pneumonia — RSV
items.first: Supportive care; no antibiotics

items.name: Hospital Acquired Pneumonia / VAP
items.workup: New CXR consolidation after 48h admission; send ETT/sputum culture, PCT, CBC, blood culture
items.aetiology: Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacter sp., Serratia marcescens, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, E. coli
items.first: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h OR Cefepime 2g IV q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Levofloxacin 750mg IV/PO q24h (penicillin allergic); if high ESBL risk start meropenem, contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

items.name: Hospital Acquired Pneumonia / VAP — MRSA positive
items.workup: Screening positive or recent MRSA culture
items.first: Vancomycin (per protocol / contact ID/Clinical Microbiology)
items.second: Linezolid 600mg PO BD

items.name: Pneumocystis Pneumonia
items.workup: Immunocompromised (HIV CD4<200, transplant, chemo, ≥20mg prednisone/day >1mo); dry cough, progressive dyspnea days-weeks; diagnose sputum PCR/DFA, Beta-D-glucan, silver stain
items.first: TMP/SMX 2 DS tabs PO q8h x21 days + prednisone (15-30min before TMP/SMX): 40mg q12h x5d, 40mg q24h x5d, 20mg q24h x11d
items.second: If unavailable, transfer to MOH

items.name: Lung Abscess
items.workup: Requires drainage, culture, adjust per culture
items.aetiology: S. aureus, Streptococcus sp., Enterobacteriaceae, Anaerobes
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD + vancomycin 1g IV BD (also if penicillin allergic)
items.second: Vancomycin + cefepime 2g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg q8h

items.name: Empyema
items.workup: Requires drainage, culture and pH, adjust per culture
items.aetiology: Acute: S. aureus, MRSA, Streptococcus sp. / Chronic: Enterobacteriaceae, Anaerobes, M. tuberculosis
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD + vancomycin 1g IV BD
items.second: Vancomycin + cefepime 2g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg q8h

items.name: Cellulitis — erythema without induration/abscess
items.first: Augmentin 1g PO BD
items.second: Cefuroxime (penicillin allergic) OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD if severe

items.name: Cellulitis — erythema with induration/abscess
items.workup: Drain abscess, culture, adjust per culture
items.first: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab PO BD OR Clindamycin 600mg PO TDS
items.second: Doxycycline 100mg PO BD OR Vancomycin if severe

items.name: Carbuncles/Furuncles/Abscess — Outpatient MRSA
items.workup: Drain and culture if abscess present
items.first: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab PO BD OR Clindamycin 450mg PO q8h
items.second: Doxycycline 100mg PO BD OR Vancomycin if severe

items.name: Carbuncles/Furuncles/Abscess — Outpatient MSSA/Strep
items.workup: Drain and culture if abscess present
items.first: Augmentin 1g tab PO BD OR Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab PO BD
items.second: Doxycycline 100mg PO BD OR Clindamycin 450mg PO q8h

items.name: Carbuncles/Furuncles/Abscess — Inpatient
items.workup: Drain and culture if abscess present
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD OR Clindamycin 450mg PO q8h
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD

items.name: Necrotizing Fasciitis
items.workup: Emergent surgical debridement, tissue culture, adjust per culture
items.aetiology: S. pyogenes, S. aureus, Clostridial sp., Anaerobic, Klebsiella sp., E. coli
items.first: Clindamycin 900mg PO q8h + Piperacillin-tazobactam + vancomycin OR + ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + vancomycin
items.second: Clindamycin 900mg PO q8h + Meropenem (if high ESBL risk) + vancomycin

items.name: Pyomyositis
items.first: Vancomycin 1g IV BD
items.second: Cefazolin 2g IV q8h

items.name: Animal Bite
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD
items.second: Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Mastitis
items.workup: Drain and culture if abscess present
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD
items.second: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab PO BD OR Clindamycin 450mg PO q8h (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Outpatient — Mild
items.workup: Debridement, tissue culture, adjust per culture
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD OR Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab PO BD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Doxycycline 100mg PO BD OR Clindamycin 300mg PO q8h

items.name: Outpatient — Mild (suspected MRSA or penicillin allergic)
items.first: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab PO BD
items.second: Doxycycline 100mg PO BD OR Clindamycin 300mg PO q8h

items.name: Outpatient — Mild (recent antibiotic exposure)
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD + ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD OR TMP/SMX 1 DS tab BD + ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD
items.second: Doxycycline 100mg PO BD + levofloxacin 750mg PO OD OR Clindamycin 300mg PO q8h + levofloxacin 750mg PO OD

items.name: Moderate-severe — No complicating features
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Cefotaxime 2g IV q8h

items.name: Moderate-severe — Recent admission (previous resistance)
items.first: Piperacillin-tazobactam OR Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Meropenem 1g IV q8h if previous ESBL

items.name: Moderate-severe — Recent admission (previous MRSA)
items.first: Piperacillin-tazobactam + vancomycin OR Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD + vancomycin (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Meropenem 1g IV q8h if previous ESBL

items.name: Moderate-severe — Limb ischemia / necrosis
items.first: Vancomycin + ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (penicillin allergic) OR + piperacillin-tazobactam (if recent admission/antibiotics)
items.second: Vancomycin + Meropenem 1g IV q8h if previous ESBL

items.name: Away from axilla or perineum
items.workup: Debridement, tissue culture, adjust per culture
items.aetiology: S. aureus, Coag-neg staph, Streptococcus sp.
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD OR Clindamycin 300–450mg PO q8h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD OR TMP/SMX 1 DS tab BD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Axilla or perineum
items.aetiology: S. aureus, Streptococcus, Gram-negative bacilli, Anaerobes
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg PO q8h OR Clindamycin (if MRSA suspected) + ciprofloxacin (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Vancomycin 1g IV BD +/- ciprofloxacin OR TMP/SMX 1 DS tab BD

items.name: GI or GU
items.aetiology: S. aureus, Streptococcus, Gram-negative bacilli, Anaerobes
items.first: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD +/- metronidazole OR Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD +/- metronidazole (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h

items.name: Trunk and Limbs
items.first: Augmentin 1 tab PO BD OR Clindamycin 450mg PO q8h OR Cefuroxime 500mg PO BD (penicillin allergic, no anaphylaxis hx)
items.second: If MRSA: Vancomycin 20mg/kg loading then 15mg/kg IV BD, trough 15–20 OR TMP/SMX 1 DS tab BD

items.name: Sepsis <7 days
items.workup: Send cultures; stop antibiotics after 48h if negative
items.aetiology: Group B strep, E. coli, Klebsiella sp., Enterobacter, Enterococcus, Enterovirus, S. aureus, Listeria sp., Salmonella sp.
items.first: Ampicillin 150mg/kg/day IV divided q8h + cefotaxime 100mg/kg/day divided q12h +/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV OD
items.duration: Stop at 48h if negative; otherwise per site of infection

items.name: Sepsis 1–4 weeks old
items.first: Ampicillin 200mg/kg/day IV divided q6h + ceftriaxone 75–100mg/kg IV OD
items.second: Ampicillin 200mg/kg/day IV divided q6h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV OD; if MRSA: vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h
items.duration: Stop at 48h if negative; otherwise per site of infection

items.name: Preterm to age <1 month
items.aetiology: Group B strep, E. coli, S. pneumoniae, Enterococcus sp., Listeria sp., Gram-negative bacilli
items.first: Ampicillin 75–100mg/kg IV q6h + cefotaxime 100–150mg/kg/day divided q8–12h (0–7d) OR 150–200mg/kg/day divided q6–8h (8–28d) + gentamicin 2.5mg/kg IV q8h
items.second: Ampicillin 75–100mg/kg IV q6h + cefepime 50mg/kg IV q8h

items.name: 1 month to 12 years
items.aetiology: S. pneumoniae, Meningococci, H. influenzae, Listeria monocytogenes, S. agalactiae, E. coli
items.first: Cefotaxime 225–300mg/kg/day IV divided q6–8h + vancomycin 60mg/kg/day divided q6h (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Ceftriaxone 100mg/kg/day IV q12h + vancomycin 60mg/kg/day divided q6h

items.name: Cystitis/Lower UTI >3 months
items.aetiology: E. coli, Klebsiella sp., Enterobacter, Enterococcus sp.
items.first: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 10–15mg/kg PO q8h OR Cefixime 8mg/kg PO OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Ceftriaxone 75–100mg/kg IV OD

items.name: Asymptomatic Bacteriuria
items.aetiology: E. coli, Klebsiella sp., Enterobacter, Enterococcus sp.
items.first: No need to treat

items.name: Acute Otitis Media — Viral (6mo–12y)
items.first: No antibiotics needed

items.name: Acute Otitis Media — Bacterial, no antibiotics in prior month/no recurrent AOM/no conjunctivitis
items.aetiology: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis
items.first: Oral amoxicillin 80–90mg/kg/day divided q8–12h OR amoxicillin-clavulanate extra-strength 90/6.4mg/kg/day divided q12h

items.name: Acute Otitis Media — Bacterial, prior antibiotics/failed amoxicillin/recurrent/purulent conjunctivitis
items.aetiology: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis
items.first: Amoxicillin-clavulanate extra-strength 90/6.4mg/kg/day divided q12h OR IV ceftriaxone 50mg/kg IV/IM OD x3 days
items.second: Levofloxacin 20mg/kg divided q12h if other options failed

items.name: Tonsillitis/Pharyngitis — Typically viral
items.first: No antibiotics; symptomatic treatment only

items.name: Tonsillitis/Pharyngitis — Bacterial
items.aetiology: S. pyogenes, Streptococcus sp., Mycoplasma pneumoniae
items.first: Oral amoxicillin 50mg/kg q24h (max 1000–1200mg) OR amoxicillin-clavulanate 45mg/kg/day divided q12h
items.second: Azithromycin 12mg/kg q24h OR clarithromycin 15mg/kg/day divided q12h (penicillin allergic)

items.name: CAP — Neonate <1 month, Viral (RSV)
items.first: Supportive care; no antibiotics

items.name: CAP — Neonate <1 month, Bacterial
items.workup: Send blood/urine culture, LP, CBC, RSV, influenza
items.aetiology: Group B strep, E. coli, S. pneumoniae, S. aureus, Listeria
items.first: Ampicillin 150mg/kg/day IV divided q8h + cefotaxime 100mg/kg/day divided q12h +/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV OD
items.second: Vancomycin if MRSA positive, 60–80mg/kg IV divided q6–8h (penicillin allergic)

items.name: CAP — Child 1–3 months, Outpatient
items.first: Oral amoxicillin 90–100mg/kg divided q8–12h
items.second: Azithromycin 10mg/kg x1 (max 500mg), then 5mg/kg q24h (max 250mg) (penicillin allergic)

items.name: CAP — Child 1–3 months, Inpatient
items.first: If febrile: IV cefotaxime 50mg/kg q6–8h
items.second: IV ceftriaxone 75–100mg/kg/day OD; if afebrile: IV azithromycin 10mg/kg x1 then 5mg/kg q24h (penicillin allergic)

items.name: CAP — Child >3 months, Outpatient
items.aetiology: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae
items.first: Oral amoxicillin 90mg/kg/day divided q12h
items.second: Azithromycin 10mg/kg x1 then 5mg/kg q24h x4 days (penicillin allergic)

items.name: CAP — Child >3 months, Inpatient (fully immunized)
items.aetiology: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae
items.first: IV ampicillin 150–200mg/kg/day divided q6h
items.second: Cefotaxime 150mg/kg/day divided q8h (penicillin allergic)

items.name: CAP — Child >3 months, Inpatient (NOT fully immunized)
items.workup: Adjust per culture; switch IV→PO when improving
items.aetiology: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae
items.first: IV ceftriaxone 75–100mg/kg/day OD (penicillin allergic)
items.second: Cefotaxime 150mg/kg/day divided q8h; add vancomycin 60–80mg/kg q6–8h if community MRSA concern

items.name: Viral Pneumonia — Influenza A&B
items.first: Oseltamivir weight-based: 2wk–11mo 3mg/kg/12h; ≤15kg 30mg/12h; >15–23kg 45mg/12h; >23–40kg 60mg/12h; >40kg 75mg/12h
items.second: No antibiotic needed

items.name: Viral Pneumonia — RSV, 0–12y
items.first: Supportive care as needed; no antibiotic needed

items.name: Abdominal aorta reconstruction / groin-incision leg procedures / prosthesis-inserting vascular procedures / lower extremity amputation for ischemia
items.comments: If the patient is already receiving antibiotics that cover likely pathogens, prophylactic antibiotics are not needed.

items.name: Ophthalmic surgery (general, e.g. cataract surgery)
items.comments: Addition of cefazolin 100mg by subconjunctival injection, or intracameral cefazolin 1–2.5mg or cefuroxime 1mg at end of procedure, is optional.
items.firstLine: Topical neomycin–polymyxin B–gramicidin OR 4th-generation topical fluoroquinolone (gemifloxacin/moxifloxacin), 1 drop q5–15min x5 doses

items.name: Biliary tract/pancreatic — high-risk laparoscopic or open procedure only
items.comments: High risk: age>70, pregnancy, acute cholecystitis, nonfunctioning gallbladder, obstructive jaundice, bile duct stones, immunosuppression. Low-risk laparoscopic procedure: no prophylaxis needed.

items.name: Gastroduodenal — lumen entered (gastrostomy, pancreaticoduodenectomy) or not entered (vagotomy, reflux procedures)
items.comments: High-risk: morbid obesity, obstruction, decreased motility, decreased gastric acid, bleeding, cancer/debilitation.

items.name: Appendectomy
items.comments: If ruptured viscus: continue therapy 5 days.
items.alternatives: Clindamycin/Vancomycin + Ciprofloxacin/Levofloxacin/Gentamicin + Metronidazole (if clindamycin not used)

items.name: Colorectal surgery
items.alternatives: Clindamycin/Vancomycin + Ciprofloxacin/Levofloxacin/Gentamicin + Metronidazole (if clindamycin not used)

items.name: Cesarean delivery — intact membranes/not in labor
Hysterectomy / Gyn-oncological / laparotomy procedures (omentectomy, oophorectomy)
items.comments: No prophylaxis needed for: diagnostic laparoscopy, tubal sterilization, cystoscopy, hysteroscopy, IUD insertion, endometrial biopsy, oocyte retrieval, surgical treatment of miscarriage (except septic), cervical biopsy/LEEP/endocervical curettage.

items.name: Pelvic organ prolapse / mid-urethral sling / vaginal repair / 3rd–4th degree perianal tear / vesicovaginal or rectovaginal fistula
items.alternatives: Clindamycin/Vancomycin + Ciprofloxacin/Levofloxacin/Gentamicin + Metronidazole (if clindamycin not used)

items.name: Embryo transfer
items.comments: Routine antibiotic prophylaxis is not recommended.

items.name: Urologic surgery (general)
items.comments: If recent/previous UTI, consider covering the isolated pathogen if possible. Single-dose gentamicin may be added for placement of prosthetic material.

items.name: Clean operation involving hand, knee, or foot, not involving fixation of foreign material
Spinal procedures with or without instrumentation
Endocarditis prevention — prosthetic cardiac valve/material, previous IE, congenital heart disease, cardiac transplant valvulopathy, or any gingival/periapical manipulation or oral mucosa perforation
items.comments: Not recommended for: anesthetic injections (unless through infected area), dental X-rays, shedding of primary teeth, orthodontic appliance adjustment/placement, bleeding from lip/oral mucosa trauma.
items.firstLine: Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid (Cefazolin or Ceftriaxone if unable to take oral medication)

items.name: Clean, with prosthetics
items.comments: No prophylaxis needed for uncomplicated/minor clean procedures: tympanoplasty/otoplasty, septoplasty, turbinoplasty, stapedectomy, tonsillectomy, adenoidectomy.

items.name: Clean-contaminated (e.g. major ear surgery, complex septorhinoplasty)
Clean with risk factors, or clean-contaminated
items.comments: Risk factors: implants, skin irradiation before the procedure. No prophylaxis needed for: reduction mammoplasty, mammoplasty, lumpectomy, prophylactic mastectomy.

items.name: Clean with risk factors, or clean-contaminated
